transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. How can I help you today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. I feel like the future has just kind of closed in on me, like there isn’t much to look forward to anymore. It just feels really hard to imagine things being any different than they are right now.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in most activities that you used to enjoy?

Yes, I really have. I've stopped going to my pottery classes, skipped hiking outings with friends, and just let my garden go completely untended. Even an art road trip I planned recently ended up feeling like an obligation rather than something to look forward to.
Have you had previous episodes of feeling this way, and if so, how long did they last?

No, I haven't really experienced this kind of persistent, heavy feeling before this current period started about two years ago. Before that, I was generally quite active and content. This constant sense of grayness is really new to me.
Have you had any periods during the past two years where you felt completely back to your usual self, with no symptoms of depression for at least several weeks?

No, I haven't had any breaks from it at all. This heavy, drained feeling has been constant and steady for a little over two years now, starting shortly after my bank merged. I haven't felt like my usual self even for a week during this whole time.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [F32, F33], which correspond to single and recurrent major depressive episodes, respectively. However, based on the patient's report of a persistent, low-grade depressed mood lasting for over two years with no symptom-free intervals of even several weeks, major depressive disorder (F32/F33) is less likely, as such episodes typically involve a complete remission between episodes. The chronic, unrelenting course without relief suggests a more enduring depressive condition, specifically dysthymia (persistent mood disorder), which is classified under F34.1 in ICD-10. Therefore, the differential has been revised to F34.1 as the most consistent with the clinical presentation.

The nonspecific nature of the distress and possible chronicity also raises consideration of mixed anxiety-depressive disorder (F41.2) or adjustment disorder with depressed mood (F43.2). Additionally, the pervasive sense of pessimism and limited future outlook could reflect underlying personality vulnerability (F60). No information yet rules out any of these; thus, all remain as initial differential candidates.
